introduction: Today we celebrate the Ascension of the Lord. Forty days after his Resurrection, Jesus leads his disciples out to Bethany, lifts up his hands and blesses them, and is carried up into heaven. They return to Jerusalem with great joy. The Letter to the Hebrews tells us that Christ has entered heaven to appear before God on our behalf. Let us lift our eyes to Christ in glory, and then go out as his witnesses.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Christ has entered heaven to appear before God on our behalf. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may proclaim repentance and forgiveness in Christ's name to all the nations. Let us pray to the Lord.
For missionaries and all who bear witness to Christ in difficult places: that they may be clothed with power from on high. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who feel abandoned or alone: that they may know that Christ blesses them and intercedes for them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For Christian unity: that all the baptized may hold fast to the hope we confess. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that, like the apostles, we may return to our daily lives with great joy and praise. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Almighty Father, your Son has entered heaven, where he lives to intercede for us. Fill us with joy and hope, and send us out as his witnesses. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: While he blessed them
reflection.body:
Luke tells the Ascension twice: at the end of his Gospel and at the beginning of the Acts of the Apostles. It is both an ending and a beginning.

In Acts, the risen Jesus has spent forty days with his disciples, "speaking about God's Kingdom." They still ask about an earthly kingdom: "Lord, are you now restoring the kingdom to Israel?" Jesus redirects them: "But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth."

In the Gospel, the last image of Jesus on earth is a blessing. "He led them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands and blessed them. While he blessed them, he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven." Jesus leaves with his hands raised over his friends, and in a sense they remain raised over us still.

What do the disciples do? We might expect them to be sad. Instead, "They worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy, and were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God." They understand that Jesus has not abandoned them. He has gone ahead.

The Letter to the Hebrews explains what he is doing now. Christ entered "into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us." And so we can approach God with confidence: "let's hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering; for he who promised is faithful."

The Ascension is our hope: where Christ has gone, we hope to follow. And it is our mission: we are his witnesses now. This week, remember that Christ blesses you, and pray for the Holy Spirit to give you courage to be his witness where you live and work.
